painting.definition: A picture made with paint and shown on a wall.

sculpture.definition: A three-dimensional work of plastic art.

statue.definition: A carved figure made to look like a person or animal.
statue.exampleUsage: The statue was identified during the lesson.

portrait.definition: A drawing or painting of a person.

landscape.definition: A picture showing natural scenery such as hills or fields.

mural.definition: A large picture painted directly on a wall or ceiling.

mosaic.definition: A picture or design made from small pieces placed together.

pottery.definition: Ceramic ware made from clay and baked in a kiln.

artifact.definition: A man-made object taken as a whole.

skeleton.definition: The internal supporting structure that gives an artifact its shape.

mummy.definition: A body embalmed and dried and wrapped for burial (as in ancient Egypt).

gallery.definition: A room or space where works of art or historical objects are displayed.

exhibition-hall.definition: A large room or gallery used to display artworks, objects, or themed exhibitions.
exhibition-hall.exampleUsage: The sculpture collection filled the exhibition hall.

lobby.definition: A large entrance or reception room or area.

rotunda.definition: A large circular room, often under a dome.

courtyard.definition: An area wholly or partly surrounded by walls or buildings.

archive.definition: A collection of records kept for future reference.

storage-room.definition: A designated room for organizing and keeping supplies, materials, or equipment until they are needed.

auditorium.definition: The area of a theater or concert hall where the audience sits.

gift-shop.definition: A retail shop offering a varied selection of items suitable for giving as presents.

cafe.definition: A small restaurant where drinks and snacks are sold.

cloakroom.definition: A room where coats and other articles can be left temporarily.

restroom.definition: A public room containing toilets and washing facilities.

ancient.definition: Belonging to times long past especially of the historical period before the fall of the Western Roman Empire.

medieval.definition: Relating to or belonging to the Middle Ages.

renaissance.definition: The period of European history at the close of the Middle Ages and the rise of the modern world.

colonial.definition: Relating to a period when a place was controlled by another country.

revolution.definition: A drastic and far-reaching change in ways of thinking and behaving.

empire.definition: A group of countries under a single authority.

dynasty.definition: A sequence of powerful leaders in the same family.

archaeology.definition: The branch of anthropology that studies prehistoric people and their cultures.

civilization.definition: A society in an advanced state of social development (e.g., with complex legal and political and religious organizations).

monument.definition: A structure erected to commemorate persons or events.

ruins.definition: The remains of a building or place that has been damaged or destroyed.

tomb.definition: A place for the burial of a corpse (especially beneath the ground and marked by a tombstone).

display-case.definition: A glass-fronted cabinet used to display special objects.

pedestal.definition: A raised base that supports a statue or other displayed object.

frame.definition: The supporting shape or structure of a building.

label.definition: A brief description given for purposes of identification.

plaque.definition: (pathology) a small abnormal patch on or inside the body.

spotlight.definition: A strong focused light that shines on one part of a stage.

velvet-rope.definition: A soft rope barrier, often attached to posts, used to keep visitors away from restricted areas or objects.
velvet-rope.exampleUsage: A velvet rope kept visitors back from the fragile display.

audio-guide.definition: A recorded or digital guide that provides information about exhibits as visitors move through a museum.
audio-guide.exampleUsage: The audio guide explained the history of the painting.

brochure.definition: A small book usually having a paper cover.

catalog.definition: A book or pamphlet containing an enumeration of things.

timeline.definition: A display showing historical events in the order they happened.

interactive-screen.definition: A digital display that responds to touch or other user input.
interactive-screen.exampleUsage: The interactive screen showed a map of the ancient city.

curator.definition: The custodian of a collection (as a museum or library).

guide.definition: A person who shows visitors around and explains what they see.

visitor.definition: A person who goes to a place for a short time.

guard.definition: An adult who watches children to keep them safe.

artist.definition: A person whose creative work shows sensitivity and imagination.

historian.definition: A person who is an authority on history and who studies it and writes about it.

restorer.definition: A skilled worker who is employed to restore or refinish buildings or antique furniture.

admiring.definition: Showing that you respect someone and think highly of them.

sketching.definition: The activity of making quick or preliminary drawings.
sketching.exampleUsage: Visitors were allowed to do pencil sketching in the gallery.

photographing.definition: The activity of taking photographs with a camera or other device.
photographing.exampleUsage: The museum sign explained where photographing was permitted.

donating.definition: Giving money, things, or other help to people or groups, often to help others.

exploring.definition: Examining places or traveling through them to learn more about the world.
